stepNotes.1: The unit owns catalog and policy construction in agent.ts plus deterministic topic routing and optional complexity classification in router.ts.
stepNotes.2: Permission ordering, environment-file reads, external directories, nested fanout, and provider-bound generation prompts define the security boundaries.
stepNotes.3: Initialization and default selection preserve their invariants, but Agent.get asserts a non-optional type over a lookup that deliberately returns undefined.
stepNotes.4: Instance caching and parallel policy loads bound startup cost; routing is fixed-size, while keyword regexes are currently rebuilt for each message.
stepNotes.5: Catalog assembly, scoring, and session side effects have separate owners, with target existence checked only at the integration boundary.
stepNotes.6: Classifier cleanup is defensive; generated identifiers still lack an empty-result guard and contain one removable self-assignment.
stepNotes.7: Sixty-three focused tests cover policy and routing behavior, with generation and mocked classifier failure/timeout paths left uncovered.
stepNotes.8: No Critical or High item exists; the empty ledger is consistent, and the optional-return mismatch is recorded as a Low contract concern.
stepNotes.9: Both focused Vitest files passed all 63 tests, and the core package typecheck completed without errors.
